title: break, continue and loop else
summary: Leave a loop early, skip a round, and find out whether a loop finished normally.

intro.text:
Two words change how a loop flows:

- `break` leaves the loop **at once**. The rest of the block and all later rounds are skipped.
- `continue` skips the rest of **this round** and goes on to the next one.

Both usually sit inside an if. A common pattern is `while True:` with a break inside: repeat until something happens.

`pass` does nothing at all. It fills a spot where Python needs a line but you have nothing to do yet.

A loop can have an `else:` too. It runs when the loop ends normally, and is **skipped when the loop was left with break**. That makes searches neat: break when you find it, and the else means "not found". The loop panel marks the rounds where break or continue ran.
intro.analogy: Searching the pockets of your coats for your keys, one coat at a time. Found them? Stop searching (break). An empty coat? Move straight on to the next one (continue). Checked every coat without finding them? That is the loop else: time to look somewhere else.

predict.q: What does this print? Type it exactly.
predict.why: 1, 2 and 3 are printed. When n is 4, break leaves the loop before the print.
For even numbers continue skips the print and goes to the next round, so only 1, 3 and 5 are printed.
The break never runs, so the loop ends normally and its else block runs.

quiz.q: When does a loop's else run?
options: When the loop ends without a break
When the loop's test is True

quiz.why: It is a placeholder for where Python needs a line.

quiz.q: How does a `while True:` loop end?
quiz.why: The test never changes, so a break is the way out.

quiz.q: `for i in range(5):` with `if i == 2: break` and then `print(i)`. What prints?
quiz.why: At i == 2 the loop is left before printing.

mistakes.title: break outside a loop
mistakes.explain: break only means something inside a for or while loop. To skip code here, use if and else.

mistakes.title: continue before the counter changes
mistakes.explain: When n is 2, continue jumps back to the test before n += 1, so n stays 2 forever. Update the counter before the continue.
